# Dustloft

> A free, open-source macOS app that shows what is hidden inside "System Data"
> and reclaims it without deleting anything that cannot be recovered.

Dustloft measures every real consumer of disk space on a Mac, sorts findings into
three tiers (regenerable, needs-admin, permanent), and shows every item with its
full path and real size before anything is removed. MIT licensed, no subscription,
no account. It sends one anonymous line when its reclaimed total changes, and
once a day even when it has not — a random identifier
belonging to that copy of the app, its total bytes reclaimed, and its version —
which can be switched off in the app. Nothing about the contents of a disk ever
leaves it.

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS 13 or later, universal binary (Apple Silicon and Intel)
- Price: free, MIT licensed
- Source: https://github.com/kapil303196/dustloft
- Install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kapil303196/dustloft/main/install-online.sh | bash

## What it refuses to do, by design

- Never deletes a .git directory. It offers `git gc` and flags repositories whose
  history exists on no remote (verified with `git ls-remote`).
- Never touches Dropbox, iCloud Drive or any cloud-synced folder, because a local
  delete there propagates to every device.
- Never removes Docker volumes. Unused images and stopped containers only.
- Never claims to reclaim "purgeable" space, which no third-party app can
  reliably free.

## Guides

- [Why is System Data so large on your Mac?](https://dustloft.com/blog/why-is-system-data-so-large-on-mac): What the System Data label actually contains, with measured sizes from a real 512 GB Mac.
- [How to clear System Data on a Mac](https://dustloft.com/blog/how-to-clear-system-data-mac): Step-by-step with exact Terminal commands, and what must never be deleted.
- [Free CleanMyMac alternatives](https://dustloft.com/blog/free-cleanmymac-alternatives): Honest comparison of the free tools and what each is good at.
- [Docker.raw taking up space on Mac](https://dustloft.com/blog/docker-raw-taking-up-space-mac): Why apparent size and allocated size differ for sparse files.
- [Find large files on Mac using Terminal](https://dustloft.com/blog/find-large-files-mac-terminal): The du, df and mdfind commands that work, and the glob mistake that hides tens of GB.
- [What is purgeable space on a Mac](https://dustloft.com/blog/purgeable-space-mac): Why no third-party app can free it on demand, and what genuinely reduces it.
- [Is it safe to delete ~/Library/Caches?](https://dustloft.com/blog/is-it-safe-to-delete-library-caches): Safe but rarely useful; the large folders are Application Support and Containers.
- [WhatsApp and Messages media on Mac](https://dustloft.com/blog/whatsapp-messages-media-mac): Received media lives in Group Containers, is real data rather than cache, and does not regenerate.
- [node_modules and build output](https://dustloft.com/blog/node-modules-taking-up-space-mac): Measuring dependency trees, and why a dist folder inside node_modules is the package itself.
- [Xcode DerivedData, simulators and runtimes](https://dustloft.com/blog/xcode-derived-data-simulators): The four Xcode paths, which need admin, and why they survive uninstalling Xcode.
- [Git repositories taking up space](https://dustloft.com/blog/git-repositories-taking-up-space): Repack with git gc; a configured remote is not proof anything was pushed.

## Reference

- [What Dustloft refuses to do](https://dustloft.com/safety): The complete list of protected locations, the three safety tiers, and the reasoning behind each rule.
- [What Dustloft sends](https://dustloft.com/privacy): The literal request body, field by field, what happens to the IP address, and the two ways to switch it off. Also covers this website's own analytics, which are separate from the app.

## Notable technical findings documented here

- `du -sh ~/*` silently skips every hidden folder because the shell glob does not
  match dotfiles. On one machine this hid 55 GB.
- Docker.raw is sparse: it can report 494 GB apparent size while occupying 9.3 GB.
  `du` reports the truth, `ls -lh` does not.
- A GitHub remote being configured does not mean a repository is backed up.
  `git ls-remote origin` returning zero refs means nothing was ever pushed.
- Simulator runtimes under /Library/Developer/CoreSimulator are installed outside
  the Xcode app bundle, so they survive deleting Xcode and are then orphaned.
- WhatsApp keeps received media in
  ~/Library/Group Containers/group.net.whatsapp.WhatsApp.shared/Message/Media.
  It is data, not cache: nothing regenerates it.
- Purgeable space is released by macOS on its own schedule. No supported API lets
  a third-party app trigger that release.
